la:verb:exhaurio.gloss: to draw out, empty by drawing, deplete
senses: to draw out, empty by drawing, deplete

la:verb:exhaurio.html:
ex-haurĭo, hausi, haustum, 4, v. a. (
fut. part. act. exhausurus, ), to draw out, to empty by drawing, to exhaust (class., esp. in the transf. and trop. senses).
Lit., of liquids: cum alii malos scandant, alii per foros cursent, alii sentinam exhauriant,pump out,; cf. : vinum,i. e. to drink up,: exhausto jam flumine, cf.: exhaustum poculum,emptied,: exhaustus repente perennis exaruit fons,; cf.: tacent exhausti solibus amnes,.—
Transf., of things not liquid, to take out, empty out, to make empty, to exhaust: terram manibus sagulisque,: humum ligonibus,: pecuniam ex aerario,; cf. aerarium,i. e. to empty, exhaust,; : praedam ex agris urbibusque sociorum,; cf.: oppidum diripiendum militi dedit: exhaustis deinde tectis ignem injecit,completely pillaged, Drak.: reliquum spiritum,; cf. infra, and Halm ad loc.: exhauriri,drained of money impoverished,: provinciam sumptibus et jacturis,: plebem impensis (aedificandi),: socios commeatibus,: heredem legatis,: facultates patriae,; cf. vires,: genas,i. e. to make bloodless, pale,: velut exhausta pullulet arca nummus,.
Trop. (according as the notion of taking away or of leaving empty predominates).
To take away, remove: libentius omnes meas laudes ad te transfuderim, quam aliquam partem exhauserim ex tuis,: alicui dolorem,: sibi manu vitam,; cf. : exhausta vis ingens aeris alieni est,cleared off,: Scurra exhausto rubore (i. e. pudore),: ad multorum exhaurienda peccata,.—
To exhaust, bring to an end: tantus fuit amor, ut exhauriri nulla posset injuria,be exhausted,; cf.: amicorum benignitas exhausta est in ea re,: unius ambulationis sermone exhaurire (quae sollicitant anguntque), to exhaust in speaking, i. e. to discuss thoroughly, ; cf. : exhaustus est sermo hominum,: deinde exhauriri mea mandata,to be accomplished, fulfilled,, 13, 3; cf.: mandavi omnia, quae quidem tu, ut polliceris, exhauries,: labores,to endure, undergo,: laborem, periculum, Drak.; 25, 31, 7; 26, 31, 7; ; . 236 al.: bella,: vastae pericula terrae,; cf.: dura et aspera belli,: poenarum exhaustum satis est,executed, inflicted,: exhausta nocte,spent,: exhaustus cliens,worn out,.

exhortātĭo, ōnis, f.
exhortor
,
an exhorting, exhortation, encouraging (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic.): quae tua exhortatione excepi, Planc. ap. ; : strepere cuncta clamoribus et tumultu et exhortatione mutua,; et saep.—In plur., ; ; —With obj. gen.: studiorum,.

la:verb:exhorresco.html:
exhorresco, rŭi, 3,
v. inch. n. and a. [exhorreo].
Neutr., to tremble or shudder exceedingly, to be terrified (class.): non possum non exhorrescere, si quid intra cutem subest vulneris, Planc. ap. : in quo igitur homines exhorrescunt?: metu,: oraque buxo Pallidiora gerens exhorruit aequoris instar,: omnis spiris exhorruit arbor,.—
Act., to tremble or shudder at any thing, to be terrified at, to dread (poet.): vultus amicos,: furores,: verbere candentes armos,; .

la:verb:exhalo.html:
ex-hālo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
Act., to breathe out, exhale, evaporate (class.): exhalantque lacus nebulam,: nebulam, fumos,; : caliginem,: mortiferum spiritum,; cf.: pruina jam exhalata,: edormi crapulam et exhala, let the fumes pass off, i. e. get sober, : crapulam,; cf. ; Lucil. ap. ; cf. : odores (ara),: flammam (Aetna),: animam (i. e. vitam),to die,; 6, 247; 7, 861; 11, 43: omni bellorum pompa animam exhalare opimam,; so, vitam,: supremam lucem,: animas,.—
Neutr.
To breathe out, i. e. expire: hic illic, ubi mors deprenderat, exhalantes,: invenitur aliquis qui velit perire membratim quam semel exhalare?.—
Transf., to steam (poet. and very rarely): vapore altaria,: exhalant vestes,.
la:verb:exhalo.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:verb:exhortor.html:
ex-hortor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. a. (act.: exhortavit,; pass.: exhortantur,: exhortatus est,), to exhort, encourage (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Prop.: trepidosque obitumque timentes,; cf.: trepidos cives in hostem,: tauros in illum,: se in ambos,: sese in arma,; cf. : Graeco sermone ad spem,: milites ad ultionem,.—With ut, ; ; ; cf. with simple subj.: juvenes nostros exhortatus es, consulatum circumirent,.—With inf.: semetipsos hortantur vel aliquas partes earum addiscere,.—Absol.: in alloquendo exhortandoque,.—
Transf., with abstr. objects, to stimulate, excite any thing: virtutes exhortabor,: parsimoniam,; cf.: haec exhortare,.

la:verb:exhibeo.gloss: to hold forth, present, show, exhibit, display, reveal
senses: to hold forth, present, show, exhibit, display, reveal
to deliver, give up, produce; furnish, supply, provide, render
la:verb:exhibeo.html:
ex-hĭbĕo (ex-ibeo, v. Brix. ad ), ŭi, itum, 2, v. a.
habeo; lit., to hold out, reach out; hence
,
To hold forth, tender, present; to deliver, give up, produce (class.; syn.: praebeo, porrigo, praesto, tribuo, ministro, do, dono, dedo, etc.).
Lit.: ait Praetor: QVEM HOMINEM DOLO MALO RETINES, EXHIBEAS.... Exhibere est in publicum producere, et videndi tangendique hominis facultatem praebere; proprie autem exhibere est extra secretum habere, and 3, § 8: jam periculum est ne cogantur ad exhibendum formulam accipere, i. e. to acknowledge legal notice, etc. : alicui omnia integra,: exhibe librarium illud legum vestrarum,: pallium,: tabulas testamenti,: rationes,: fratres exhibe,; so, fugitivos apud magistratus,: aliquem apud acta,: debitorem in judicium, quadringentos senatores ad ferrum, et saep.: vias tutas,i. e. to make safe,: toros,i. e. to furnish, allow,: exhibuit querulos ore gemente sonos,uttered,.—
Transf.
To show, to display, to exhibit: exhibuit gemino praesignia tempora cornu,: notam linguae,: exhibuit linguam paternam, displayed, i. e. used the language of her father, : faciem sucumque,: malui me tribunum omnibus exhibere quam paucis advocatum,: se ministratorem alicui,: se adorandum adeuntibus, (but not in , where the right reading is praebuit, v. Halm. ad h. l.).—In the latter (reflexive) sense sometimes without se: quid me putas populo nostro exhibiturum?how I shall exhibit, show myself,; cf.: qui vere civilem virum exhibeat,shows, proves himself, Spald.; : pro fratre hostem exhibuit,.—
To show, confer (late Lat.): alicui honorem,.—
To maintain, support, sustain (post-class.; esp. freq. in jurid. Lat.): si quis a liberis ali desideret, vel liberi, ut a parente exhibeantur,; so, aliquem,; ; cf.: Scythas alimentis,: vitam,; .
To show, exhibit, employ; to procure, occasion, cause: rem salvam exhibebo,I will set it all right,: quorum virtus exhibet solidum decus, Phaedr. 4, 23, 24: vocis fidem, Epil. 9: munificentiam,: liberalitatem, clementiam, comitatem,; cf.: liberalitatem et justitiam,: vicem spodii,i.e. to supply the place of,; cf.: vicem testamenti,: humanitatem,to exercise, exhibit,: diligentiam,: imperium,to exercise,: alicui molestiam,to cause,; ; : negotium hominibus,to produce, occasion,; cf.: qui deum nihil habere ipsum negotii (dicunt), nihil exhibere alteri,; : negotium alicui,; ; ; ; and once reflexively: jam se exhibebit hic mihi negotium,will present itself,: argutias mihi,: difficilem laborem alicui,: curam alicui, et saep.

la:verb:exhilaro.html:
ex-hĭlăro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to gladden, cheer, to make merry or joyous, to rejoice, delight, exhilarate.
Prop. (rare but class.): miraris tam exhilaratam esse servitutem nostram?; ; .—
Transf., of things: neque ilex, picea, larix, pinus ullo flore exhilarantur,are refreshed, enlivened,: colorem hominis frequentiores in cibo lupini exhilarant,freshen, brighten,; cf.: species mulieris exhilarat faciem viri sui,.
